A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Var-RUOT work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across the changed formatting and numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on three-gene simulations and single-cell datasets, including baseline comparisons, training-speed measurements, ablations and held-out-time evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, growth-penalty and loss-norm studies, longer-horizon extrapolation and comparisons with traditional transport solvers.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 changes the specified growth regularization: the middle branch gains g(-δ), and the negative branch changes from g(λ) to g(-λ). This is a localized procedural formula change; the single-potential architecture, particle dynamics and main losses remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed accordingly.

E1.justification: v2 adds human embryoid-body and NeurIPS Challenge donor data, 150-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, and balanced/unbalanced two-dimensional reference transport scenarios. It also extends the three-gene evaluation to substantially longer extrapolation horizons. The datasets and scenarios evaluated in v1 are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add OTCFM, UOTCFM and WLF. Table 4 also adds MIOFlow, SF2M and PISDE to the existing hematopoiesis comparison. New comparisons include MMFM and Metric FM in Table 21 and traditional POT and static WFR solvers in Appendix C.5.

E3.justification: New protocols include training on t=0–4 and testing on t=5–8, constructing five pseudotime groups for the NeurIPS donor data, feature standardization, and transport validation with σ=0. These are added experimental designs; the retained experiments keep their Wasserstein metrics, convergence threshold, epoch cap and Table 6 settings.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds sensitivity to growth-penalty exponents and L1-versus-L2 loss comparisons, and extends the loss-weight ablations from EMT to hematopoiesis. v2 also adds long-horizon extrapolation tests and an HJB-loss training curve diagnosing incomplete satisfaction of the optimality condition.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five-run means and standard deviations in Appendix B.2, and v2 continues this practice in its added benchmark tables. No increased run count, new seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Previously reported rows in Tables 1–4 and the held-out-time tables are retained, but v2 adds extensive benchmark, ablation and extrapolation results. For example, new Table 17 reports t=8 W1 of 0.4260 for Var-RUOT versus 0.5047 for DeepRUOT, but W2 of 0.5557 versus 0.5362, showing mixed relative performance under the new setting.

T1.justification: The central optimality theorems and Appendix A.1 proofs remain substantively unchanged. v2 adds finite-particle convergence arguments in Appendix D.2, including Monte Carlo rates and a dimension-dependent Wasserstein-error bound, and derives the growth-potential relation for general penalty exponents in C.2. Appendix A.2 also revises the regularization formula.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contribution statements and central conclusion retain the same claims: solving RUOT through one scalar potential, obtaining lower-action dynamics with faster and more stable training, and connecting growth penalties to biological priors. Additional experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for exponent-dependent training stability, long-horizon deterioration in a time-dependent model, and discrepancies from traditional solver actions. It explicitly discusses nonzero HJB residuals as a limitation. Some added interpretation is inconsistent: C.2 reverses Theorem 4.2's growth-direction implication, and C.4's broad NeurIPS superiority statement exceeds Table 20's mixed results.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and Appendix A.3 guidance on particle counts, integration step size, higher-order integration, mass normalization and Hutchinson trace estimation. It documents preprocessing for the new datasets. These are recommendations and disclosures, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun; v1's explicit Gaussian sampling counts are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions Var-RUOT as generalizing Action Matching to simultaneous stochastic and unbalanced dynamics. New Appendix D.1 and Table 23 substantially expand comparisons of architectures, losses, intermediate-distribution requirements and supported properties. Additional references support the new datasets, numerical guidance, convergence discussion and traditional solver comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain. v2 refines terminology and related-work wording, adds a non-autonomous-system remark, expands the conclusion, and inserts a discussion appendix before the relocated limitations. This is a limited reorganization rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS template substantially changes typography, text width and display sizing. Main trajectory figures are redrawn with expanded marker explanations; v1's ablation Figures 7–8 become v2's Tables 9–10. Figure 5 gains panels, and new benchmark tables, a method-comparison table and an HJB-loss plot are added. Other appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Additional baselines, quantitative high-dimensional evaluations, sensitivity tests and longer extrapolation make the empirical support more informative, while computational guidance and a code link improve reproducibility documentation. However, new inconsistencies limit the gain: C.2 contradicts the growth-direction theorem, Table 8 disagrees with retained modified-metric results, and the NeurIPS superiority statement overstates Table 20. The unchanged central evidence and useful added tests support a modest net improvement, rather than an unqualified substantial one.
